findings.title: The specification overstates stdin delivery as already proven live
findings.criterion_ref: SPEC3-T08 — prior live-proof language must not assert an already-approved production guarantee beyond what was actually observed.
findings.trigger: An implementer relies on v3's claim that the corrected projection-delivery mechanism was already proven live and omits the pending stdin transport validation.
findings.consequence: The Claude worker's canonical input delivery can fail in production despite the specification representing that mechanic as proven.
findings.evidence: §7.2 lines 922–926 says how the projection reaches the worker was “proven live,” and §19 line 1771 labels stdin projection delivery as proven live. However, N20 evidence `23_claude_stream_json_identity_events.log` records a trailing `<instruction>`, not the required JSON stdin projection; N20-F04 says stdin was an approved design choice still requiring resolution/proof. The recovery plan §“Validate before implementation,” items 3–4, explicitly leaves successful stdin delivery and projected-schema acceptance to future validation.

observations: The historical v1/v2 hashes match the required digests, and v3 contains zero case-insensitive `gemini` or `google` substring matches.

The approved model/effort mapping is correctly reproduced in §20.2, but stale language elsewhere still calls `USER_DECISION_REQUIRED-01` open (§7.1, §19, and §21). This was not raised as a separate blocking finding because the resolution was not silently omitted, though the status language should be reconciled.

The transport requirements themselves cover inline CLI-schema projection, stdin delivery, per-turn `message.model` extraction, and initialization-event tool/MCP inspection with flag-only evidence rejected.
reasoning: I compared v3 against v2, checked the immutable-spec hashes and retired-term scan, inspected the four corrected transport mechanisms, and checked their cited N20 evidence and recovery plan. The substantive mechanics satisfy SPEC3-T03–T06, and no prohibited architecture/topology drift survived review. The remaining major issue is the explicit live-proof overclaim: the evidence proves schema flag behavior, stream identity, and observed tool/MCP state, but not the newly required stdin projection delivery that v3 calls proven.
